transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-18 15:00 UTC, duration ~48m. Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Laura Mendes (Redwood CSM); Alice Moreno (Procurement), Dr. Ben Carter (CTO), Evelyn Park (Security), Sam Ortiz (Legal).

Summary: quick procurement/legal kickoff focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets for Dedicated (uptime/latency), pricing approval process for finance, and onboarding timeline. Redwood to send docs and schedule legal review workshop.

Topics: MSA/DPA, SLAs (99.9% uptime, latency targets), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, pricing deck, SOC2 and pen test, KMS integration, pilot plan.

00:00 Jared: All right good afternoon everyone thanks for making time, this is Jared from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Laura from customer success.
00:12 Alice: Hi thanks Jared, Alice here from VanguardMed procurement, looks like we've got our legal and security folks on as well.
00:18 Ben: Ben Carter, CTO, I'll be mostly scoping perf and infra questions.
00:22 Evelyn: Evelyn Park, security and compliance, I'll focus on SOC2, data residency and KMS.
00:27 Sam: Sam Ortiz, legal. We'll be reviewing the MSA and DPA redlines.
00:32 Priya: Hi team, quick note on flow - Jared will run through procurement asks, I'll cover technical SLAs and perf, then we can go into redlines and next steps.

02:05 Jared: The objective of today's call is simple - align on MSA/DPA requests, SLA targets, pricing approvals and an onboarding/pilot plan. Alice, maybe start with your procurement checklist so we can make sure we hit everything.
02:20 Alice: Sure, procurement is looking for an executed MSA and DPA, list of security artifacts (SOC2, pen test), confirmation of data handling (no persistent storage for PHI unless contracted), proof of insurance, and the pricing approval flow - we need a vendor packet to start finance approval. Timelines: procurement wants to be vendor approved by end of May ideally.
02:45 Jared: Got it, end of May vendor approval. We'll prioritize the MSA/DPA redlines. For the MSA we generally see a few common asks - liability caps, indemnity, IP, and data ownership. Sam, what are your major redlines so we can address them now?
03:05 Sam: Primary asks are mutual indemnity on third-party claims, limitation of liability adjustments, and a clause on data return or deletion post-termination with certification. Also standard audit rights.
03:20 Jared: Understood. Our standard MSA includes a deletion certificate clause and we're fine to conversation on liability cap, can you share target cap ranges?
03:32 Sam: For mid-market healthcare, procurement is asking for a cap at 2x fees for the first year and carveouts for gross negligence. We'll redline with specifics.

04:10 Priya: On the technical side, Ben, can you confirm what SLA numbers you're after? Are you thinking 99.9% availability and a 99th percentile latency target? Also is Dedicated capacity the route you prefer?
04:27 Ben: Yes we need predictable latency for real-time clinical assistant features, 99.9% is our baseline ask, and 99th pctl under 300ms for token generation would be ideal but we can be flexible. Dedicated preferred for data isolation and consistent throughput.
04:40 Priya: Thanks. For Dedicated we can commit to an SLA that includes throughput guarantees per instance pool and target P99 latency ranges; I will share our benchmark numbers. Note that p99 token gen at 300ms depends on model choice & sequence length.
04:55 Ben: Sure, model choice matters - we're planning a mix of embeddings for search plus a smaller generation model for assist.

06:00 Evelyn: A few security things - SOC2 Type II report, latest penetration test report, encryption at rest with customer KMS/HSM, key rotation policy, access logs and audit trail retention (we need 1 year), SSO/SAML and RBAC controls. Also data residency, our primary data centers are in US East.
06:24 Priya: We can provide SOC2 and a pen test summary; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for on-prem-style connectivity. Note: sometimes the transcription system shows product as 'Redwood Dedicatad' but it's Redwood Dedicated.
06:40 Evelyn: Regarding KV cache - we need to understand if any short-term caching persists and how it's encrypted.
06:46 Priya: Good question, our runtime does prefix and KV caching to speed inference, caches are ephemeral and encrypted; for Dedicated we can provide more exact retention windows and policies. I'll include a diagram in the doc.

08:10 Jared: On pricing - Alice, what's the approval path? Who signs off and is there a procurement committee?
08:17 Alice: Finance + Legal + IT security need to approve. Target approvers: CFO (pricing), Head of Engineering (scale), and Legal. We'll need a formal vendor packet with MSA/DPA, pricing, and insurance to start.
08:30 Jared: Understood. Our pricing options: hosted pay-as-you-go or Dedicated reserved capacity with monthly commit. Dedicated pricing includes reserved instance pricing and options for burst. We'll send a pricing spreadsheet with line items for reserved v CPU/GPU counts, burst credits, and estimated token costs.

10:00 Sam: On the DPA side, we need clarity on subprocessors and cross-border transfers - VanguardMed maintains some EU customers, so data transfer mechanics matter.
10:12 Priya: Our DPA lists subprocessors by region; for EU data we can route to EU region instances. We'll include region routing and an explicit subprocessors list in the packet.

12:00 Ben: About Dedicated networking - can you support V P C peering and private connectivity? We need to limit egress and ensure private IP routing.
12:10 Priya: Yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options. For on-prem we also offer Redwood Private which can be air-gapped; that has additional lead time.
12:20 Ben: Lead time for Private?
12:22 Priya: Typically 8-12 weeks for full on-prem deployment; Dedicated can be spun up in 2-3 weeks depending on capacity reservations and SLA negotiation.

14:00 Alice: For the pilot, procurement wants a 30-day pilot with limited production usage to validate. Finance will require estimated costs and likely a PO for the pilot.
14:12 Jared: We can do a 30-day Dedicated pilot. We'll include estimated token consumption and a not-to-exceed number for finance to process a PO.

16:00 Evelyn: Encryption questions - KMS integration and whether Redwood ever sees plaintext keys; also audit logs for key use.
16:10 Priya: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private, Redwood never stores plaintext keys. Key usage logged and we'll provide audit entries.

18:00 Jared: On insurance - we can provide proof of insurance; I'll attach cert. Any minimums you require?
18:08 Alice: Standard liability and cyber insurance minimums, we'll include numbers in the vendor packet template, but 5 million is usual for cyber.

20:00 Sam: Timelines - procurement needs vendor packet by 2026-04-23 to review before the committee meets. Legal can then schedule a workshop the following week.
20:12 Jared: We'll target to send docs by 4/23. Priya will supply perf docs earlier if possible.

22:00 Priya: Quick technical note - when we talk about p99 latency it's based on steady state load; cold starts can add jitter, but with Dedicated warm pools that's minimized. We'll share test harness results.
22:30 Ben: Good, we need a test harness to run our sample prompts to validate. Will you run a joint benchmark?
22:36 Priya: Yes we can run a joint benchmark; I'll set up a test plan and we can schedule a run during the pilot.

25:00 Alice: A question on data deletion post-termination - we need either certification of deletion or the ability to pull logs for audit.
25:10 Jared: Our DPA includes deletion certification; we'll make sure the MSA and DPA align here.

28:00 Evelyn: Retention of logs - you mentioned 1 year, can that be configurable?
28:10 Priya: For Dedicated we can configure audit log retention windows; we'll note options and costs.

30:00 Sam: A legal workshop would be helpful to walk our redlines. Can Redwood legal attend?
30:06 Jared: Yes we'll have Redwood legal join; propose sometime the week of 4/27.
30:15 Sam: Works for us.

32:00 Priya: Competitor note - we often see customers evaluate with OpenAI or Anthropic. One difference is our Dedicated and Private options which give more control over keys and tenancy. Just calling that out since you mentioned CloudProviderX earlier.
32:25 Ben: Understood, control and predictable latency matter more to us than marginal cost savings.

34:00 Alice: For the pricing spreadsheet we need line items and a not-to-exceed pilot number. Finance also asks for payment terms - net 30 vs net 45.
34:10 Jared: We'll include both options; typically we offer net 30, but can accommodate net 45 for enterprise contracts.

36:40 Priya: I'll attach our Dedicated runbook and a sample benchmark for p50/p95/p99 numbers across typical sequence lengths. Also a short diagram on KV cache and how ephemeral storage is handled.
36:55 Evelyn: Good, would like the diagram and the KMS integration details.

39:00 Jared: Let's recap real quick - action items: Redwood sends redlined MSA/DPA and pricing spreadsheet by 2026-04-23; Priya shares perf benchmarks and a test plan by 2026-04-22; schedule legal workshop week of 4/27; provide SOC2 and pen test; agree pilot NTE cost and start after MSA execution.
39:30 Alice: That matches procurement expectations. We'll review and return any initial comments.

41:00 Sam: One more - subprocessors list should be included in DPA and indicate whether any subprocessors process EU data.
41:10 Priya: We'll include region routing and subprocessors by region.

43:00 Ben: When can we expect the onboarding timeline if pilot approved?
43:08 Laura: From signed MSA to pilot start typically 10 business days for Dedicated provisioning plus configuration; full onboarding docs and runbook will be provided in advance.

45:00 Jared: OK thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with the packet and a calendar invite for the legal workshop. Any final questions?
45:12 Evelyn: None from security for now.
45:15 Alice: No, thanks.
45:18 Ben: Good session.
45:22 Jared: Thanks all, talk soon.

Transcript notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicatad' vs Dedicated, 'K V cash' for KV cache) and speaker overlap. Links shared during call: pricing spreadsheet (link to shared drive), SOC2 report (link), pen test summary (link).
